# htmltags — DSL cheat sheet

Greenfossil's Scala 3 HTML templating engine. Typed tag/attribute builders that
render HTML server-side. `README.md` has the tutorial; this file is the quick
reference.

```scala
import com.greenfossil.htmltags.*
```

## Tags

```scala
div("hello")                       // <div>hello</div>
html(head(title := "My Page"), body(h1("Hi")))   // nested; head/body are PairedTag
br                                 // <br/>
img(src := "/a.png")               // <img src="/a.png"/>
```

`PairedTag("div")` (`<div>…</div>`), `UnPairedTag("br")` (`<br/>`), `StartTag("meta")`
(`<meta>`, never content). Tags are values; `tag(label, nodes*)` builds a custom
one. Modern semantic tags include `search(...)` and the Web Components `slot(...)`.

## Attributes

```scala
div(cls := "card", id := "c1")     // <div class="card" id="c1"></div>
h1(backgroundColor := "blue")     // <h1 style="background-color: blue;"></h1>
input(tpe := "text", value := "x", disabled)   // boolean flag: name only
```

Plain attributes (`attr("x")`) render `x="v"`; CSS attributes (`cssattr("x")`)
fold into a `style="…"` block. `hidden`, `inert`, `checked`, `disabled`,
`autofocus`, `selected`, `multiple`, `required`, … are no-value flags. Modern
attributes include `popover`, `popovertarget`, `popovertargetaction`, `command`,
`commandfor`, `enterkeyhint`, `inputmode`, `fetchpriority`, `decoding`,
`shadowrootmode`, `shadowrootdelegatesfocus`, `part`. `slot` is in `Attrs2`
(because a `slot` tag also exists).

All attributes are statically typed [[Attribute]] values; the binding fixes the
HTML name, and call sites use `:=` rather than an attribute-name string.

### Attribute-name casing

- **Hyphenated HTML attributes and CSS properties → camelCase Scala binding.**
  Preserve the hyphen in the emitted name: `val httpEquiv =
  attr("http-equiv")`, `val acceptCharset = attr("accept-charset")`,
  `val borderColor = cssattr("border-color")` (CSS properties fold into
  `style="…"`).
- **HTML attributes with no hyphen stay lowercase** (`colspan`, `rowspan`).
  **SVG attributes keep their spec casing** (`viewBox`, `preserveAspectRatio`).
- **ARIA is the exception.** The `aria-*` suffix is a single lowercase token, so
  typed names mirror it exactly: `aria.labelledby`, `aria.describedby`,
  `aria.haspopup`, `aria.valuenow` — never `aria.labelledBy`.
- **Dynamic `data.*` / `aria.*` suffixes are verbatim.** Use nested dynamic names
  for `data-*` hyphens: `data.request.id` → `data-request-id`.

Dynamic namespaces (`Node.scala`):

```scala
div(data.placeholder := "hi")      // <div data-placeholder="hi"></div>
span(aria.label := "Menu")         // <span aria-label="Menu"></span>
section(aria.labelledby := "title", aria.describedby := "question")
                                   // <section aria-labelledby="title" aria-describedby="question"></section>
span(aria.autocomplete := "list")  // dynamic fallback for an unlisted name
svg(xmlns("svg") := "...")         // namespace helper
```

`data.*` and `aria.*` emit `prefix-<suffix>` via `Dynamic`. A nested dynamic
expression composes with hyphens, so no raw attribute string is needed:

```scala
div(data.click.count := 0)          // <div data-click-count="0"></div>
div(data.request.id := "r1")        // <div data-request-id="r1"></div>
div(data.wb.last.activity := "...") // <div data-wb-last-activity="..."></div>
```

`data.*` accepts the normal value lattice (String, Int, Boolean, Option, Seq, …);
see `DataAttributeSuite`. Common ARIA names (`label`, `labelledby`,
`describedby`, `hidden`, `live`, `current`, `expanded`, `pressed`, `controls`,
`haspopup`, `modal`, `valuenow`, …) are typed `val`s whose names mirror the exact
lowercase suffix; any other `aria-*` name remains available through the dynamic
fallback and is appended verbatim. Prefer these namespaces over
`attr("data-…")` / `attr("aria-…")` in new code.

## The `:=` value lattice — `AttributeValueType`

The RHS of `attr := _` accepts (`Extensions.scala`):

```
String | Int | Long | Double | Float | BigDecimal | Boolean     // scalar
CSSUnit | RawText | AttributeValueLike                          // special
Option[scalar] | Seq[scalar]                                    // collections
```

- `CSSUnit`: `20.pt`, `1.5.rem`, `50.pct` (`.px .pt .pct .mm .cm .in .pc .em .ch
  .ex .rem .deg .grad .rad .turn`).
- `Option`: `None` → renders nothing (attribute omitted); `Some(v)` → `v`.
- `Seq`: space-joined (e.g. class lists).
- `String` and every scalar are escaped on render (see below).

## Extending the value type — `AttributeValueLike` (the seam)

```scala
trait AttributeValueLike:
  def render: String

case class Money(cents: Long) extends AttributeValueLike:
  def render: String = f"${cents / 100.0}%.2f"

div(price := Money(1999))          // <div price="19.99"></div>
```

Implement `def render: String` and the value is assignable with the ordinary
`:=` — **no core change, no escaping surprise** (the rendered string is escaped
like any attribute value). This is the sanctioned extension seam for a binding
library to carry a domain value through.

**Reference implementation:** htmx's `HxJsonAttribute` (`hx-vals` / `hx-config` /
`hx-headers`) — a JSON-valued attribute built on this seam. JSON (`JsValue`,
`Json.obj`) lives in `commons-json`, *not* here: `htmltags` stays dependency-clean
(see `AGENTS.md` — JSON is a binding-library concern).

## Escaping (and the `raw()` trap)

- **Text nodes** escape six characters: `"`→`&quot;`, `'`→`&apos;`,
  `<`→`&lt;`, `>`→`&gt;`, `&`→`&amp;`, `/`→`&#x2F;`.
- **Default attribute values** escape only `"` and `'` (`&quot;` / `&apos;`);
  `<`, `>`, `&`, `/` pass through verbatim.

```scala
p("<script>alert('x')</script>")
// <p>&lt;script&gt;alert(&apos;x&apos;)&lt;&#x2F;script&gt;</p>
```

- `attr(name, renderValueAsEscape = false)` opts an attribute out of escaping.
- **`raw(text)` / `RawText` bypasses escaping entirely** — the XSS trap. Wrap
  only trusted, self-produced markup (or already-correct content that must not
  be escaped twice).

## Conditional rendering

```scala
div(1 to 5 map (i => ifTrue(i > 2, p("Paragraph ", i))))    // only i > 2
div(1 to 5 map (i => ifFalse(i > 2, p("Paragraph ", i))))   // only i <= 2
```

Overloads exist for `Tag`, `Attribute`, `Node`, and `String`.

## Interpolator

```scala
val n = 3
htmltags"<p>${n} items</p>"        // args are rendered (escaped) via anyToNode
```

## Forms — `Form.scala`

```scala
form(method := "POST", action := "/save", enctype := "multipart/form-data")
input(tpe := "hidden", name := "csrf", value := token)

import com.greenfossil.htmltags.Form
Form.hidden("csrf" -> token)                 // Seq[Tag] of hidden inputs
Form.text("q" -> "hi")                       // Seq[Tag] text inputs
Form.inputs("a" -> 1, "b" -> "x")            // (name, value) tuples
Form.urlencoded("/save")(Form.text("q" -> "hi")*)   // full form
Form.multipart("/upload")                    // multipart form
```

`(String, AttributeValueType)` and `(String, String, AttributeValueType)` have
`given Conversion`s to `FormInputType`, so tuples can be passed directly.

## CSS selectors — query & transform

```scala
val frag = div(p("1"), p("2"), p("3"))
frag.cssQuery("p:first-child")               // Seq[Tag]
frag.addNodes("div.target", p("new"))        // insert
frag.deleteTags("#third-paragraph")          // remove
frag.replaceNodes("p", span("x"))            // replace matched
frag.modifyAttribute(".p", cls, modFn)       // edit an attribute
```

## Rendering

```scala
frag.render                        // compact HTML String
frag.prettyPrint                   // pretty-printed DOM String
Seq(nodeA, nodeB).render           // render a Seq[Node]
"<p>x</p>".toDom.prettyPrint       // String → DOM → pretty
```

`anyToNode` (used by the interpolator) flattens `Option`/`Seq`/`Try`, maps
`null`/`Nil` → nothing, and falls back to `toString` for other types.
